mechanism: "shrinkdebugfile" is a DEFINE-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS row (src/config-options.lisp:450) and the only other occurrence of "shrink" in src/ is our own SHRINK-LOG-FILE. START-FILE-LOGGING (src/node/logging.lisp:141-152) takes PATH and nothing else and calls (shrink-log-file path) unconditionally at :146 before opening the file; %INIT-LOGGING calls it at src/node/init.lisp:133, ahead of APPLY-LOG-CATEGORIES at :171, so the -debug categories are not even applied yet at the point the scroll happens. SHRINK-LOG-FILE itself is a faithful port of Core's ShrinkDebugFile (refs/bitcoin/src/logging.cpp:514-545): the same 10,000,000-byte tail at the same 11 * (RECENT_DEBUG_HISTORY_SIZE / 10) threshold. Core puts a gate in front of it that we do not have: StartLogging runs it only when GetBoolArg("-shrinkdebugfile", LogInstance().DefaultShrinkDebugFile()) is true (refs/bitcoin/src/init/common.cpp:108-113), and DefaultShrinkDebugFile() is (m_categories == BCLog::NONE) (refs/bitcoin/src/logging.cpp:167-170) -- so a node started with ANY -debug category does not scroll its log, and -shrinkdebugfile=0 keeps it whole in every case.
consequence: The operator debugging an intermittent fault runs with -debug=net and restarts to reproduce it; the restart discards everything past the last 10 MB of the evidence -- exactly the case Core's default excludes -- and -shrinkdebugfile=0 does not stop it either, because that option is accepted and ignored. This is the row where the dimension's mitigation is weakest in the -debug direction: Core DERIVES the default from -debug, so an operator who supplies only -debug supplies no option we can warn about, and nothing is printed (the survey's class-(c) blind spot). It stays S3 and not higher: the loss is retrospective log evidence, never node state or funds, it only bites on logs already past 11 MB, the operator who does type -shrinkdebugfile=0 IS warned (measured), and the reverse direction is safe -- we never grow an unbounded file across restarts, whereas Core under -debug does.
evidence: Executed in the project container (worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-options-s3, warm image, probe ga11probe/p-rest.lisp, function P-SHRINK; *log-file-stream* and *log-file-path* saved and restored, and confirmed back to NIL afterwards). A 12,000,000-byte file was written, (enable-log-category "net") was called and confirmed ((log-category-enabled-p "net") => T, the state in which Core's DefaultShrinkDebugFile() returns false), then BITCOIN-LISP::START-FILE-LOGGING was called on that path: bytes before 12,000,000, bytes after 10,000,000 -- the log was scrolled anyway. (sb-introspect:function-lambda-list #'start-file-logging) => (PATH): there is no argument that could carry the gate. (bl.cfg::core-only-option-p "shrinkdebugfile") => T, and START-NODE-PLIST on an argument list including -shrinkdebugfile=0 returned (:LISTEN T :WALLET-NAMES NIL :NETWORK :REGTEST) with "shrinkdebugfile" in SUPPLIED-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS. Sources: src/config-options.lisp:450; src/node/logging.lisp:103-152; src/node/init.lisp:118-135, 164-172; refs/bitcoin/src/init/common.cpp:43,108-113; refs/bitcoin/src/logging.cpp:167-170, 514-545.
fix_shape: Give START-FILE-LOGGING Core's gate as an argument rather than a global: change it to (start-file-logging path &key (shrink t)) and have %INIT-LOGGING compute SHRINK the way Core does -- the value of a new real DEFINE-OPTION "shrinkdebugfile" row when it was supplied, otherwise (null debug-categories), Core's DefaultShrinkDebugFile() -- passing the already-available DEBUG-CATEGORIES parameter. Do not reorder %INIT-LOGGING to apply the categories before opening the log: the file has to exist before the deferred config lines are flushed, and the raw -debug list is already in scope at src/node/init.lisp:133. Leave SHRINK-LOG-FILE itself alone; it already matches ShrinkDebugFile byte for byte. A test should write a file past the threshold and assert it is scrolled with no -debug category and left whole both with a category supplied and with -shrinkdebugfile=0, using the no-category case as the positive control so a broken gate that never scrolls cannot pass.
